name: Taiwan Strait military pressure
started: 2022-08-04 (Fourth Taiwan Strait Crisis: large PLA drills began after US Speaker Pelosi's visit)
summary: No shots have been fired, but China keeps rehearsing a blockade of Taiwan. Its December 2025 'Justice Mission-2025' drill put live-fire zones inside Taiwan's territorial waters for the first time since 2022 and fired 27 rockets toward the island's approaches, and in June 2026 Chinese ships ran the first 'law enforcement patrols' off Taiwan's east coast, which analysts read as a quarantine rehearsal.

sides.name: People's Republic of China
members: PLA Eastern Theater Command (ground, navy, air and rocket forces)
sides.strength: Justice Mission-2025 peak: 130 aircraft, 14 warships and 8 other official ships in 24 hours (Taiwan MND, 30 Dec 2025); separate Dec 2025 drill involved 90+ ships.

sides.name: Taiwan (Republic of China)
backers: United States (arms sales; a package of over $11 billion approved Dec 2025)

background: Since August 2022 the PLA has staged a series of large exercises around Taiwan (Joint Sword in 2023 and 2024, Strait Thunder-2025A in April 2025), each one practising blockade of ports such as Keelung and Kaohsiung, joint fire strikes and control of sea and air space, while daily air and naval patrols have eroded the median line. Beijing also uses its coast guard to assert 'law enforcement' around Kinmen and Matsu.

This matters because each drill brings PLA forces closer to Taiwan with shorter warning, blurring the line between exercise and the opening moves of a real blockade, while disrupting civilian air and sea traffic and testing US and Japanese responses.
year: In about 9 to 12 December 2025 China staged a drill with more than 90 ships that appeared aimed at the whole First Island Chain. After the US approved arms sales worth over $11 billion, the Eastern Theater Command launched Justice Mission-2025 on 29-30 December: ground, naval, air and rocket forces simulated blockading Keelung and Kaohsiung, an amphibious assault group of four ships operated east of Taiwan, rocket launchers on Pingtan fired 27 rockets into waters north and southwest of Taiwan, and 857 international flights were affected. Fishing-vessel formations of 2,000+ (25 December) and 1,400+ (8-13 January 2026) boats stretched 466 km in the East China Sea. From 27 February to 13 March 2026 Chinese warplanes almost disappeared from Taiwan's vicinity, a lull some analysts linked to a planned May 2026 Trump-Xi summit; patrols resumed on 14 March. China closed parts of the Yellow and East China seas for 40 days (27 March to 6 May). KMT chair Cheng Li-wun met Xi Jinping in April. From 6 to 10 June PLA Navy and coast guard ships conducted the first 'law enforcement patrols' east of Taiwan, with four large vessels coming within 32 nautical miles of the east coast and hailing civilian ships.
situation: As of late October 2026 there is no active fighting; Chinese pressure continues through patrols, coast guard activity and periodic large drills. No named major PLA exercise around Taiwan in 2026 was confirmed in sources retrieved for this research.
technical: Justice Mission-2025 day 1 (29 Dec 2025, 3 pm): 14 PLA warships, 14 CCG vessels, a 4-ship amphibious assault strike group southeast of Taiwan, 89 aircraft of which 67 entered Taiwan's response zone (Taiwan MND via Wikipedia).
24 hours to 6 am on 30 Dec 2025: 130 PLA aircraft, 14 military ships and 8 other Chinese official ships (Taiwan MND via Wikipedia).

Rockets: 27 rockets fired from Pingtan Island into waters north and southwest of Taiwan, landing near Taiwan's 24 nm line; ETC released video of a PCH-191 launcher; first rocket fire into the strait since 2022; no missiles overflew Taiwan, unlike 2022 (Wikipedia).
Exercise zones grew from five to seven and extended into Taiwan's territorial waters for the first time since the 2022 drills (Wikipedia).
First deployment of an amphibious assault ship formation in such a drill, east of the island, practising 'seizing key ports' (China Daily, citing PLA experts).
CCG announced patrols near Matsu and Wuqiu (Kinmen) during the drill (Wikipedia).
Civil impact: 100,000+ travellers expected affected, 857 international flights affected and 84 domestic flights cancelled (Wikipedia).
Strait Thunder-2025A (1-2 Apr 2025): 76 aircraft and 15 warships on day 1; 59 aircraft and 23 warships on day 2 (Wikipedia).
Fishing-vessel formations: 2,000+ boats on 25 Dec 2025 and 1,400+ on 8-13 Jan 2026, each about 466 km long, in the East China Sea (Wikipedia).
June 2026 'law enforcement patrols' east of Taiwan: first PLAN participation there; four large vessels within 32 nm of the east coast; Jamestown called it a 'quasi-quarantine' (Wikipedia).
Air activity pause: no PLA warplanes reported near Taiwan from 27 Feb to 13 Mar 2026 except on 7 Mar (Wikipedia).
Taiwan lost an F-16V in a training accident off Hualien on 6 Jan 2026 (Wikipedia: 2026 in Taiwan).

timeline.event: Large PLA drill with 90+ ships begins (about 9 to 12 Dec).
Justice Mission-2025 begins; 89 aircraft and 28 ships counted on day 1.
27 rockets fired from Pingtan; zones extend into Taiwan's territorial waters.
PLA warplanes largely vanish from around Taiwan until 13 Mar.
40-day airspace closures in Yellow and East China seas begin (to 6 May).
First PLA Navy and coast guard 'law enforcement patrols' east of Taiwan (to 10 Jun).

outlook: Watch for the next named PLA exercise, typically triggered by US arms sales, transits or speeches by President Lai, and for any move from drills to coast guard 'inspections' of shipping, which would mark a shift from rehearsal to quarantine.

battles.name: PLA Navy and coast guard 'law enforcement patrols' east of Taiwan
sides: PLA Navy and China Coast Guard
battles.outcome: Four large Chinese vessels came within 32 nm of Taiwan's east coast and hailed civilian ships.
battles.forces: Four large PLAN and CCG vessels.
battles.significance: First such patrols east of Taiwan and first with PLA Navy participation; analysts called it a 'quasi-quarantine' rehearsal that targets the side of Taiwan facing the Pacific and US reinforcement routes.

battles.name: Exercise Justice Mission-2025
battles.place: Taiwan Strait and waters north, southwest, southeast and east of Taiwan
sides: PLA Eastern Theater Command and China Coast Guard
battles.outcome: Two-day blockade rehearsal concluded; no shots fired at Taiwanese forces.
battles.forces: Ground, naval, air and rocket forces: up to 130 aircraft, 14 warships, 14 CCG vessels, a 4-ship amphibious assault group; PCH-191 rocket launchers on Pingtan fired 27 rockets.
battles.losses: None. 857 international flights affected and 84 domestic flights cancelled (Wikipedia).
battles.significance: First drill with a stated aim of deterring outside intervention; first live-fire zones inside Taiwan's territorial waters since 2022; a response to a US arms package of over $11 billion.
